headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure from residential users to large energy consumers, primarily data centers, to address rising electricity demand and costs.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger, residential ratepayers, state regulators, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, Sen. Louise Lucas.
news_headline: Virginia requires data centers to pay for grid infrastructure
news_summary: Virginia has mandated that data centers pay for their dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure, a move aimed at easing the burden of rising electricity prices on average Virginians, which have seen a 76% increase partly due to AI data centers. This decision by state regulators and the Governor is expected to save residential customers hundreds of millions of dollars by preventing utility companies from passing on massive grid upgrade costs to all consumers.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, including reclaimed water, to give state regulators better information for water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Virginia League of Conservation Voters, environmental scientists, Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Not explicitly stated, but implied by industry-favorable amendments.
news_headline: Virginia mandates data center water use reporting
news_summary: Virginia's SB 553, along with HB 496, requires water suppliers to report the volumes of potable and reclaimed water delivered to data centers monthly or quarterly. This legislation aims to provide state regulators with better data to make informed decisions about water resources, as data center water use is a growing concern in the state.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new large data centers, including noise studies for nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to consider other environmental and historical impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Del. Joshua E. Thomas, Del. Sam Rasoul, community advocates, residents near data centers.
opponents: Not explicitly stated, but implied by additional assessment requirements for developers.
news_headline: Virginia law mandates data center noise studies
news_summary: Virginia's HB 153, which took effect July 1, 2026, requires developers of new large data centers (100 MW or more) to conduct site assessments, including noise studies, for residential units and schools within 500 feet. While it mandates studies, the law does not set specific noise limits or setbacks, leaving some residents concerned about its effectiveness.
